patch.objective: Apply the ACA Code of Ethics (2014) and the law to a counseling decision, and work through an ethical decision-making model when they conflict

sources.note: Relayed from the REQ-239 NCMHCE sessions (read 2026-11-11), not re-read for this band: the objective title is the course's own, built from this outline. Current outline; NBCC's new blueprint takes effect 2027-07-01.
The objective and secondary objectives are the course's own titles.

sources.cite: ACA Code of Ethics (2014): A.5.e personal virtual relationships with current clients; A.6.a previous relationships; A.6.b extending counseling boundaries; A.6.c documenting boundary extensions; A.11.a-b and A.12 referral, values and abandonment; H.6.a separate personal and professional online presence
sources.note: Relayed from the NCE case nce-boundary-dual-relationship, not re-read for this band; its note: The current code: counseling.org (read 2026-11-11) says the 2014 Code remains current until the Board adopts a revision. A.5.e prohibits a personal virtual relationship with a current client; A.6.b names attending a client's wedding as a boundary extension to weigh, with precautions (informed consent, consultation, supervision, documentation); A.6.c asks that the rationale, benefit and anticipated consequences be documented before the interaction when feasible.
